sims.title: Neuron
sims.description: Stimulate a neuron and watch the action potential travel along its axon, with the sodium and potassium channels opening and closing.
sims.why: The ionic basis of the action potential: the voltage-gated channels, the ions that move, and the membrane potential on a chart.

credits.team: Wendy Adams, Fanny (Benay) Bentley, Janet Casagrand, Mike Klymkowsky, Ariel Paul, Katherine Perkins
credits.qualityAssurance: Steele Dalton, Amanda Davis, Bryce Griebenow, Ethan Johnson, Elise Morgan, Oliver Orejola, Bryan Yoelin
credits.thanks: Conversion of this simulation to HTML5 was funded in part by the Ghent University.

sims.title: Membrane Transport
sims.description: Put solutes either side of a membrane and add channels and carriers: watch diffusion, facilitated diffusion and active transport.
sims.why: How solutes cross the cell membrane – through the lipid bilayer, through channels and carriers, and against a gradient with energy.

credits.team: Holly Basta, Mike Klymkowsky, Mark Nielsen, Kathy Perkins, Amy Rouinfar, Nancy Salpepi
credits.qualityAssurance: Matthew Moore, Nancy Salpepi, Valentina Pérez, Kathryn Woessner
credits.thanks: HHMI BioInteractive for supporting the design and development of this simulation.

sims.title: Diffusion
sims.description: Lift a divider between two gases and see how the number, mass and temperature of the particles change how fast they mix.
sims.why: Diffusion down a concentration gradient – the movement of gases and solutes in the body – and what makes it faster or slower.

credits.team: Jack Barbera, John Blanco, Michael Dubson, Amy Hanson, Linda Koch, Ron LeMaster, Trish Loeblein, Emily B. Moore, Ariel Paul, Dennis Perepelitsa, Kathy Perkins, Tom Perkins, Nancy Salpepi, Carl Wieman
credits.qualityAssurance: Jaspe Arias, Jaron Droder, Clifford Hardin, Matthew Moore, Liam Mulhall, Jacob Romero, Nancy Salpepi, Luisa Vargas, Kathryn Woessner

sims.title: Gas Properties
sims.description: Pump particles into a box and change its volume and temperature: see the pressure change, and the gas laws behind it.
sims.why: The gas laws (Boyle's and Charles's) that underlie breathing, the partial pressures of the gases in air, and diffusion of gases.

credits.team: Jack Barbera, John Blanco, Michael Dubson, Amy Hanson, Linda Koch, Ron LeMaster, Trish Loeblein, Emily B. Moore, Ariel Paul, Dennis Perepelitsa, Kathy Perkins, Tom Perkins, Nancy Salpepi, Carl Wieman
credits.qualityAssurance: Jaspe Arias, Jaron Droder, Clifford Hardin, Matthew Moore, Liam Mulhall, Jacob Romero, Nancy Salpepi, Luisa Vargas, Kathryn Woessner

sims.title: Under Pressure
sims.description: Fill a tank with fluids of different density and measure the pressure at different depths, with and without the air above.
sims.why: Pressure in a column of fluid (ρgh): why blood pressure differs between the head and the feet, and how pressure is measured against atmospheric pressure.

credits.softwareDevelopment: John Blanco, Aadish Gupta, Sam Reid
credits.team: Bryce Gruneich, Trish Loeblein, Ariel Paul, Kathy Perkins, Rachel Pepper, Noah Podolefsky

sims.title: pH Scale
sims.description: Measure the pH of everyday liquids, dilute them with water, and see the concentrations of H₃O⁺ and OH⁻ on a logarithmic scale.
sims.why: What pH means as a logarithmic scale of the hydrogen ion concentration, the pH of body fluids, and the effect of dilution.

sims.title: Acid-Base Solutions
sims.description: Compare strong and weak acids and bases: how much of each dissociates, and the pH and conductivity of the solution.
sims.why: Weak acids that dissociate only partly – the basis of buffers, and of the bicarbonate buffer of the blood.

sims.title: Molarity
sims.description: Change the amount of solute and the volume of solution, and see the concentration in moles per litre.
sims.why: Concentration in mol L⁻¹, and the arithmetic of making up solutions and diluting them for a practical.

sims.title: Beer's Law Lab
sims.description: Make up a coloured solution and measure how much light it absorbs as you change its concentration, the path length and the wavelength.
sims.why: Spectrophotometry: the Beer–Lambert law (absorbance = ε c l) that turns the absorbance of a solution into its concentration.

sims.title: Gene Expression Essentials
sims.description: Make proteins from a gene: transcription factors and RNA polymerase make mRNA, and ribosomes translate it.
sims.why: Transcription, its control by transcription factors, translation, and the breakdown of mRNA and protein that sets how much is made.

sims.title: Color Vision
sims.description: Mix red, green and blue light, or filter white light, and see the colour that a person perceives.
sims.why: How three kinds of cone and the mixing of their signals give colour vision, and what filters do to the light that reaches the eye.

sims.title: Geometric Optics
sims.description: Move an object in front of a lens and follow the rays to its image: change the focal length and see the image move and grow.
sims.why: How a lens forms an image – the optics of the eye and of the microscope's objective and eyepiece, and their magnification.

sims.title: Capacitor Lab: Basics
sims.description: Charge a capacitor with a battery and change the area and separation of its plates: see the charge and energy stored.
sims.why: The cell membrane as a capacitor: a thin insulator that separates charge, which is why a membrane takes time to charge (Q = CV).

sims.title: Least-Squares Regression
sims.description: Place data points and fit a straight line by eye and by least squares, and see the residuals and the correlation.
sims.why: Fitting a straight line to data – a standard curve for an assay, or a calibration – and what the residuals and r tell you.
